notes: The outcome is located, but neither the broad believer-group description nor p. 154 identifies paranormal versus religious belief. Japanese/American labels describe the respective replication samples and cannot map the original contrasts. Both original comparisons occur in this single source; row order cannot resolve correspondence. Candidate location-identification ANCOVAs, age covariate, p. 153: paranormal believers versus skeptics, partial eta squared = .143, F(1,36) = 6.01, p = .019 (exact); religious versus non-religious, partial eta squared = .127, F(1,36) = 5.26, p = .028 (exact). PDF confirms printed metric is partial eta squared, not unqualified eta squared; canonical text encodes its symbol as a control character. These tests use correct location identifications divided by correct plus incorrect location identifications on trials with a detected face. Related hit-rate tests on the same page are distinct: religious/non-religious F(1,36) = 10.15, p = .003, partial eta squared = .220; paranormal/skeptic F(1,36) = 9.99, p = .003, partial eta squared = .217. Discussion on p. 154 mentions predefined face-area hits without selecting a belief comparison. No candidate is assigned to a row. Candidate only: paranormal believers 19 + skeptics 20 = 39 participants; religious people 20 + non-religious people 19 = 39 participants. Each sum uses opposite, mutually exclusive belief quartiles within that comparison. The two comparisons overlap and must not be added together. Recruitment N = 73 and study-wide N = 47 are separate roles; middle belief scores were excluded by the upper/lower quartile restriction. No N is inferred from degrees of freedom. Model-specific additional exclusions are not stated in the located Results paragraph. These group-based N candidates are retained for parent field-scope review only. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
